content:
Tomáš Novák: Heads up for folks on rotation: we updated the Automated Region Failover runbook + on-call training deck for the new failover automation work. Please skim before your next shift.

Tomáš Novák: Runbook (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/automated-region-failover-runbook

Tomáš Novák: TL;DR changes:
- New failover orchestrator state machine + what “MONITOR_ONLY” vs “ENABLED” actually means
- Manual override endpoints + RBAC notes (who can do what)
- New dashboards: region health signals + failover transitions + customer impact by tier
- Stop conditions + rollback checklist

Tomáš Novák: I’m doing a 25 min walkthrough today 2pm PT. Drop questions here and I’ll incorporate.

incident-bot: Reminder: On-call training walkthrough scheduled by Tomáš Novák. Calendar invite: “Failover automation runbook walkthrough”.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also reminder: in prod right now we’re still mostly in MONITOR_ONLY for most routes. You’ll see “would have failed over” events. Don’t panic-page unless there’s actual customer impact or the signals are truly concerning.

Peter Holtz: Question on MONITOR_ONLY: what’s the expected action if it looks like the trigger engine would have gone to FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED? Do we proactively prep capacity in target region or just observe?

Miles Thornton: Good q. In MONITOR_ONLY the orchestrator will:
- emit state transitions + recommended actions
- NOT push routing/DNS changes

Miles Thornton: On-call action depends:
1) If impact is real (5xx/tail latency + confirmed): treat as incident; you can prep for manual failover while we validate safe-to-failover checks.
2) If impact is not real (synthetics flapping): capture in thread, tag #reliability-failover, and we’ll tune thresholds.

Aisha Bello: From alerting side: we intentionally did NOT wire paging directly off “FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED” right now. Paging remains on SLO burn / error rate / tail latency alerts. The new failover states show up as annotations on the SLO dashboard.

Connor O'Brien: For training: the runbook has a “GO / NO-GO” preflight list before any manual override. Please follow it; we’ve had too many “oops target region is at 92% GPU alloc” moments.

Ethan Park: Q: where do we check the RBAC / who has permission to hit the override endpoints? Last incident we had to route through 3 people.

Tomáš Novák: Updated in runbook under “Permissions & escalation”. Short version:
- SRE Oncall + Incident Commander can request
- Only members of “failover-operators” can execute ENABLE/DISABLE overrides in prod
- If you’re IC and not in group, page SRE manager-oncall (Rafael’s rotation) or use the #oncall-escalations path

Tomáš Novák: There’s also an internal ticket open to broaden the group slightly (INT-881), but we’re keeping it tight until after the next controlled test.

Jordan Lee: Adding a detail: override endpoints are split:
- “set_mode(MONITOR_ONLY|ENABLED)” requires elevated role
- “acknowledge_state” is allowed for oncall so you can stop repeated notifications + attach incident link

Mina Haddad: Another Q from routing side: progressive failover. If we enable, are we defaulting to 5% canary? Who chooses the customer tiers to move first?

Miles Thornton: Default policy in prod (when enabled) is:
- start 1% canary for Hosted API routes only
- then 5% / 25% / 50% / 100% with hold-down timers between stages
- Dedicated is opt-in per customer (explicit allowlist)

Miles Thornton: Tier scoping is defined in the routing policy config. The runbook says: if you’re doing manual override, do not move Enterprise/Dedicated unless (a) you have capacity confirmation from Capacity Ops and (b) Support is looped in.

Dev Patel: +1 on Support loop-in. If you’re doing anything that can change routing behavior for Enterprise customers, please post in #support-escalations with:
- which regions
- what tier
- expected symptoms
We have macros ready but need heads-up.

Peter Holtz: Dashboard question: what’s “net_probe.loss_p95” actually measuring? Is it from the edge POPs or from inside the region?

Aisha Bello: It’s from three vantage points:
- inside the region (node-to-node)
- cross-region (region-to-region)
- edge synthetic (selected POPs)

Aisha Bello: The rollup shown in the failover dashboard is the cross-region + edge synthetic weighted more heavily. Inside-region probes are a separate panel (since they can look “fine” even if upstream is broken).

Tomáš Novák: This is in the “Signals quick reference” section of the runbook now. If anything still reads like soup, tell me and I’ll simplify.

Ethan Park: What’s the expected operator response when safe-to-failover check fails? E.g. target region capacity gating blocks. Do we retry later or is there a manual bypass?

Rafael Mendes: No manual bypass for capacity gating in prod. If safe-to-failover says “NO” you have two paths:
1) mitigate in-place (load shedding, timeouts, fallback model variant) and keep traffic local
2) engage Capacity Ops + Infra to free headroom / shift non-critical workloads, then retry

Rafael Mendes: If you bypass capacity gating, you risk taking down 2 regions instead of 1.

Connor O'Brien: Re: load shedding / timeouts: please coordinate with release-oncall if you’re pushing config changes. The runbook has pre-approved knobs + rollback steps; try not to do bespoke edits at 3am.

Mina Haddad: In training can we cover the “degraded but available” path? I’ve seen folks jump straight to “fail over everything” when the right move is tightening timeouts + switching model variant.

Miles Thornton: Yep. We added a runbook section “Degraded mode (no failover)” with:
- enable request hedging only for small prompts
- cap max_tokens for free tier
- fallback from large model -> smaller verified variant for non-enterprise
- reduce queue timeouts to stop pileups

Peter Holtz: For the walkthrough, can you show an example of a full state transition timeline? I want to know what “hold-down” actually looks like operationally.

Tomáš Novák: Yep. I’ll pull screenshots from last staging game day + the first prod low-risk test. Includes:
- signal window breaches
- hysteresis clearing
- hold-down timer countdown
- rollback transition

Tomáš Novák: Also adding a “common false positive” section. We already have one: edge POP packet loss spike that didn’t correlate with region health.

Jordan Lee: One more operator note: state machine doesn’t go straight to FAILOVER. It’s basically:
HEALTHY -> DEGRADED -> FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED -> FAILING_OVER (when enabled) -> FAILED_OVER
And it can bounce back with hysteresis.

Aisha Bello: And please, when you declare incident: link the incident doc/channel in the orchestrator “ack” field. We want the audit trail to be searchable later.

Dev Patel: +1000. Support keeps getting asked “did you fail over?” and we need a single source of truth.

Tomáš Novák: Cool. I’ll incorporate these Qs into the deck.

Tomáš Novák: For folks who can’t make 2pm PT: I’ll record + drop notes here. Also if you’re on-call this week and want a 10 min 1:1 run-through, DM me.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: (reaction)

Rafael Mendes: :+1: (reaction)

Peter Holtz: :thanks: (reaction)
